comment: The operator-value half of Aerie's cluster configuration (TODO_SWARM.md Phase 3b.1).
Flux reconciles from git, and docs/ethos.md keeps operator values out of git - so the values
arrive out of band as one ConfigMap, and every Kustomization under deploy/ reaches them with
postBuild.substituteFrom. This file is the pointer half: it names each key, says where its
value comes from at provisioning time, and describes what a valid one looks like. It holds no
values, and it is structural - identical for every installation, which is why it is committed.
Consumed by scripts/k3s/Set-ClusterConfig.ps1 (renders and applies the ConfigMap) and by the
${...} substitutions in deploy/. Both halves must agree on these names, so change them here
and nowhere else. Same split, and the same reasoning, as scripts/secrets/parameters.json; the
difference is only sensitivity. Nothing here is secret, so it is applied in the clear and
printed in full in the run log, which is what makes an audit record of it worth having.
Fields:
key          - the ConfigMap key, and therefore the ${...} token manifests substitute.
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE because Flux's postBuild is a shell-style expansion.
env          - environment variable Set-ClusterConfig.ps1 reads the value from. Equal to
'key' for every entry today, and kept as its own field anyway: a future key
that collides with something a CLI already owns - the way AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
does in parameters.json - has to be able to move without renaming the
substitution token every manifest uses.
githubSource - the repository variable provision-4-cluster-config.yml maps into 'env'.
githubKind   - always 'variable' here, and that is the point: an operator value is not a
secret, so it stays unmasked and legible in run logs. Note that reading one
through ${{ secrets.X }} resolves to an empty string rather than erroring.
required     - a run fails preflight if a required value is missing.
pattern      - .NET regex every value is checked against before anything is applied, and
checked case-SENSITIVELY, which PowerShell's -match is not. A typo'd hosted
zone id, a domain with a stray scheme on it, or a replica count of 30 is
otherwise diagnosed several steps later and reads as an AWS, cert-manager or
Longhorn failure rather than as the transcription error it is.
normalize    - optional; 'lower' folds the value before it is checked. Only for values whose
case genuinely carries no meaning - a domain name is case-insensitive by RFC,
so Example.com is a correct answer that Kubernetes would nonetheless reject as
an Ingress host, and folding it is better than refusing it. A hosted zone id
is the opposite: an opaque, case-sensitive string, where folding would invent
a zone that does not exist. When in doubt, leave it out and reject instead.
hint         - appended to the failure message when 'pattern' rejects a value.
example      - a syntactically valid value. Deliberately not this installation's.
consumedBy   - the TODO_SWARM.md step that first substitutes it.
description  - what it is and where the operator got it.

keys.hint: Just the base domain - no scheme, no trailing dot, no wildcard. Case is folded for you. The wildcard is added where it is needed (dnsNames becomes *.${DOMAIN} plus ${DOMAIN}, since a wildcard does not match the apex).
keys.consumedBy: 3b.10 wildcard Certificate; every Phase 5 Ingress host
keys.description: Base domain the cluster serves. Already supplied to cd.yml as vars.DOMAIN today.

keys.hint: One address, unwrapped - not a Name <addr> pair.
keys.description: Let's Encrypt account address. Expiry notices and account recovery go here.

keys.hint: A region id, not an availability zone or a display name - us-east-1, not us-east-1a and not 'US East'.
keys.description: Region holding the /aerie SSM parameter tree. Must be the same region Provision 2 seeded into - the tree lives in exactly one, and ESO reads it by region.

keys.hint: A bare IPv4 address, with no prefix length. It must sit on the nodes' own subnet - kube-vip answers ARP for it there - and outside the DHCP pool, with no reservation of its own: the VIP has no fixed MAC, which is the whole point of it.
keys.description: Floating ingress address, chosen and verified free in Phase 3a.2. Phase 7 is what finally points pfSense Unbound at it.

keys.hint: The interface name alone - eth0, not 2: eth0 and not eth0@if2. Read it with the command in Phase 3a.3.
keys.description: Interface kube-vip advertises the VIP on in ARP mode. Identical on every node, since they are built from one golden image - if it is not, Phase 3a.3 says stop and find out why.

keys.hint: The id only, uppercase - Z0123456789ABCDEFGHIJ. The console and the API both also render it as /hostedzone/Z..., and pasting that whole path is the usual mistake; strip the prefix.
keys.description: Public hosted zone for DOMAIN, from Phase 3a.4. Naming it explicitly stops cert-manager from having to enumerate zones, which the aerie-eso and Route53 policies are not scoped for.

keys.hint: Never more than the number of nodes that exist. A volume with more replicas than nodes is permanently Degraded, and its alarms are the noise that trains an operator to ignore the real ones.
keys.description: 2 during the two-node build window; Phase 7 raises it to 3 by changing this variable and re-running Provision 4 - no commit, which is the reason this is a ConfigMap and not a manifest.
